storage_findings: qkv_proj [27136, 6144] F8_E4M3 with scale_inv [216, 48]: 8 TP ranks x (16 q heads x 192 + 192 + 128 = 3392 rows, 27 blocks of 128 with a 64-row tail). Every 128x128 block of this rank-interleaved grid has max |E4M3 code| = 448 on layers 0 and 1 (all 216x48 blocks); a global [q|k|v] reading with per-rank blocks gives 93% and a plain 212-block reading 94%.

MXFP4 nibble order: low nibble = even column. On layer 1 experts 0/1/77/200 the per-input-column norm of gate_proj correlates with the router weight's column norms (-0.14..-0.59) and with |post_attention_layernorm| (0.15..0.47) only in that order (swapped: |r| <= 0.01); down_proj column norms vs up_proj row norms: 0.47..0.58 vs |r| <= 0.04 swapped. Every 32-group's max |E2M1| is 4 or 6 (E8M0 2^(s-127) with OCP floor(log2 amax)-2 scaling).
disagreements: config moe_router_dtype=bfloat16 is not read by the reference modeling file, whose gate is float32; mlx2 follows the modeling file (float32 router).

The reference MiMoV2Model.forward calls transformers' create_causal_mask with the 5.3 keyword input_embeds (config transformers_version 5.3.0); the installed 5.17 renamed it inputs_embeds. The test runner builds the same mapping with 5.17's functions and passes it as the dict the forward accepts; the mask math (causal; kv > q - window) is transformers'.

The checkpoint (FP8 fused qkv with TP-sharded scale grids, MXFP4 experts) cannot be loaded by the reference file itself (it has no dequantization); the real-layer reference is fed weights dequantized by independent NumPy code.
